claims.statement: The ECS cluster routes ECS Exec transcripts to a dedicated encrypted CloudWatch log group; the main container and optional kube-proxy sidecar write to a separate group with distinct stream prefixes.

The create-investigation and reaper Lambdas have separately named CloudWatch log groups with configurable retention; their handlers log authorization/resource-lifecycle outcomes and task deadline/reaper results, including active-session deferrals.

On normal exit and trapped shutdown signals, the entrypoint attempts a bounded S3 sync of eligible /home/sre content to an explicit or task-specific audit prefix; it excludes OCM and kubeconfig subtrees, does not follow symlink targets, and reports failure as a warning rather than guaranteeing persistence.

The investigation audit bucket is versioned and uses compliance-mode Object Lock, blocks public access, applies AES-256 encryption, denies non-TLS requests, and can replicate cross-account; the task role is granted PutObject and ListBucket while guidance directs audit retrieval through a separate compliance read role.

Bedrock invocation logging is configured for text payloads across Bedrock Runtime callers in the account and Region, sending payloads up to 100 KB to encrypted CloudWatch Logs and larger payloads to a separate S3 bucket; image, embedding and video delivery are disabled.

The shell and LocalStack tests verify that nested OCM and kubeconfig files are excluded from the S3 sync while unrelated workspace files remain eligible, and use token/account-response canaries to check the simulated uploaded content.

The investigation reaper has its own log_retention_days-governed CloudWatch group and logs eligibility reasons, EFS cleanup, task-definition deregistration counts and summary counters. Expected ClientError, BotoCoreError and OSError backup messages avoid raw file paths and object keys, but normal backup/deletion messages and other error paths can contain identifiers, directory paths, prefixes or exception details.

Before deleting a stale investigation's EFS directory, the reap-investigations Lambda uploads a best-effort backup of that directory to the audit bucket under `<cluster-id>/<investigation-id>/reaper-final-backup/`, reusing the `.config/ocm/*`/`.kube/*` exclusions and symlink-skipping behavior of the container's shutdown sync; it refuses to delete the directory if the backup fails or times out, so the backup-then-delete ordering is an invariant rather than best-effort cleanup.

The handler falls back to GRACE_PERIOD_HOURS=72 only when its environment setting is absent, while Terraform's investigation_grace_period_hours defaults to 168 and is explicitly passed into that environment variable; operators must check configured deployed values rather than assume the handler fallback applies.

Investigation GC uses access-point creation age rather than time since the last task stopped: with no matching running task, age must strictly exceed the grace period or CreatedAt must be missing and treated as legacy state. An invalid present timestamp instead enters the staleness-error path, and the handler rechecks running tasks before cleanup.

Staging declares east and west regional workspaces; their log-group names can match because the names omit Region, whereas the audit bucket naming rule includes account and Region, so retrieval must select the account and Region explicitly.

The audit-access runbook directs users to request a separately managed rosa-boundary-audit-reader S3 role through app-interface and authenticate through SAML without --assume-uid; it explicitly requires separate CloudWatch Logs read permissions. The account-baseline guide states that this Terraform baseline does not add an audit-reader role.

The shared Bedrock logging role restricts service assumption to the source account and explicitly approved source-region ARN patterns, with staging listing us-east-1 and us-west-2; invocation-logging configurations, destinations and inline delivery grants remain regional rather than combining logs through the shared role.

deploy/regional/variables.tf defaults log_retention_days to seven days while Git-managed HCP configuration overrides this to 90 for both staging and both production regional workspaces. CloudWatch container and Lambda log groups consume this setting, so they retain 90 days wherever the workspace values have actually been applied.

The HCP Terraform map declares a production account workspace allowing Bedrock log sources in east and west, with corresponding network and regional workspaces in both Regions; the account and both network and regional workspaces declare remote execution and auto-apply, while prod AWS credentials require manual apply. The configuration alone does not prove latest run status or that audit logs are live.

This Boundary page's audit pipeline (CloudWatch/S3/Bedrock/CloudTrail, per-task session transcripts) is distinct from the Trusted Actions component's audit model: Trusted Actions logs one structured 'audit record' per API call (caller, action, target, decision, outcome) and ships it via its own CloudWatch Logs subscription filter to a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that writes to S3 under an `audit-logs/` prefix with its own Object Lock/WORM configuration, independent of Boundary's investigation bucket, log groups, and retention settings.

The create-investigation Lambda's TaskCreationRequests CloudWatch EMF metric (namespace ROSABoundary) is an operations/cost signal, not part of the audit evidence inventory: it carries no OIDC subject, request ID, investigation ID, cluster ID, task ARN, or error text, and a Lambda timeout or crash can suppress its emission entirely, so it must not be relied on as an audit record.
